title: Crüger to Müller, 4/14 December 1629
author: Peter Crüger
summary: Having worked through the *Rudolphine Tables*, Crüger tells Müller that further work on the *Astronomia Danica* is now pointless, praises the tables' methods and logarithms, and is no longer averse to elliptical orbits.

notes.note: The *Astronomia Danica* (1622) of Christian Severin Longomontanus, Tycho Brahe's assistant, built on Tycho's geoheliocentric system.

notes.on: the great orb (whether of the sun or of the earth)
notes.note: *Orbis magnus*, Copernicus's name for the earth's orbit. By adding “whether of the sun or of the earth” Crüger leaves open whether the sun goes round the earth, as for Tycho, or the earth round the sun.
*Reflexiones*: a term of the Ptolemaic theory of planetary latitudes.
Kepler's *Epitome Astronomiae Copernicanae* (1617–1621), a textbook of Copernican astronomy in questions and answers, which set out his laws of planetary motion for all the planets.
The Rudolphine Tables date the Creation, an epoch Kepler fixed partly from chronology rather than astronomy.
